correctness.rationale: Primary PDF equation (2.1) uses beta S(E+A+epsilon V), no population denominator; exposed equation and next-generation R0 are linear in beta Λ/μ. Its Tables 3/4 set Λ=μ N(0) with N(0)=59,310,000, beta=.034/.34, yet print R0=.61/6.11. Let D=1/(p+q+μ)+p/[(p+q+μ)(γ_A+μ)]+qε/[(p+q+μ)(κ+γ_V+μ+δ)]; printed R0=β N0 D, normalized R0=β D. Independent exact rational calculation using all printed parameters gave for beta .034: freq 0.6114991225346483, mass 36268012.95752999; beta .34: freq 6.1149912253464835, mass 362680129.5752999. Initial infectious weighted count yields per susceptible force 8,563,683.19/day versus .1443885/day. Primary model/table screenshots and arithmetic agree. Neither model implementation nor fitted trajectory reproducibility is inferred from missing code.

value.rationale: A factor 59,310,000 is an enormous dimensionally significant discrepancy in a calibrated model, changing its R0 from order one to hundreds of millions and its initial force of infection by the same factor. The check is not novel algebra but an independently useful, fully reproducible source-specific correction separating two possible incidence conventions; failure to flag it would mislead quantitative interpretation and published numeric reproducibility.
